title: Detection of H<SUB>2</SUB>O and OH<SUP>+</SUP> in z > 3 hot dust-obscured galaxies
question: Are H2O and OH+ emission lines detected in z>3 Hot DOGs, and what do their luminosities, profiles, extents and line ratios say about excitation by star formation versus AGN?

what.value: CO(4-3) detections, molecular gas masses and wide CO line widths of the two sources

evidence.quote: were selected to be among the most starbursting Hot DOGs, with massive molecular gas reservoirs discovered in CO(4$-$3) (Fan et al. 2018)
Based on the total gas masses estimated by (cite: Fan18)

what.value: SED decomposition: AGN torus dust temperature 450 K and star-formation dust temperatures 51 K and 63 K; AGN fractions of the IR luminosity (87% and 77%)

evidence.loc: The H2O and OH+ line ratios of Hot DOGs
evidence.quote: similar to what is found for our Hot DOGs with 87% and 77% in W0149$+$2350 and W0410$-$0913, respectively (cite: Fan16b)

evidence.loc: Excitation of the H2O and OH+ emission
evidence.quote: we expect an AGN torus dust temperature of 450 K, and a dust temperature due to star-formation of 51 K and 63 K

external_data.citation: Tsai et al. 2015 (cite: Tsai15); Fan et al. 2016b (cite: Fan16b)

what.value: Literature H2O and L_IR comparison samples (low and high-z ULIRGs, SMGs, AGN) for Fig. 6

evidence.loc: The H2O-IR luminosity ratio of Hot DOGs
evidence.quote: Here we compare the two detected Hot-DOGs of this paper to low and high-$z$ ultra-luminous IR galaxies (ULIRGs), sub-millimetre galaxies (SMGs) and AGN in the literature.

evidence.quote: line ratios of 0.4 (cite: vanderWerf10; Papadopoulos07), and an $\rm OH^+(1_{1}-0_{1})/H_2O(3_{12}-3_{03})$ ratio of 0.65 (cite: vanderWerf10; Liu17)

evidence.loc: Excitation of the H2O and OH+ emission
evidence.quote: used modelling to determine the physical conditions and excitation mechanisms needed for the H$_2$O transitions of low, medium, and high energy transition

recipe.goal: Reduce, image and continuum-subtract the cubes
recipe.method: Pipeline-reduced data, natural-weighted imaging, continuum subtraction with line-free channels, 60 km/s channels

recipe.goal: Estimate emission extent and extract spectra
recipe.method: Moment-0 map of each line, imfit for size estimate, spectrum extracted from a region equal to two times the size estimate

recipe.goal: Fit line profiles and derive fluxes and luminosities
recipe.method: Single versus double Gaussian fits to H2O; for W0410-0913 a simultaneous fit of a double Gaussian CO(9-8) and a single Gaussian OH+; integrated flux for lower limit when truncated (W0149+2350)
key_parameters: Central velocity of each CO component restricted within 400 km/s and of OH+ within 200 km/s of expected value
assumptions: OH+ assumed to be in emission based on the observed spectrum

recipe.goal: Compare spatial extents of H2O, CO(9-8) and OH+
recipe.method: Velocity-limited moment-0 maps (-300 to 750 km/s for W0149+2350, -500 to 500 km/s for W0410-0913) fitted with imfit, sizes converted to kpc

recipe.goal: Constrain H2O excitation with radiative transfer
recipe.method: Non-LTE RADEX modelling using peak fluxes of H2O and CO(9-8)
assumptions: Spherical symmetry; AGN torus dust temperature 450 K, star-formation dust temperatures 51 K and 63 K

recipe.goal: Compare line-to-IR luminosity and line ratios with literature
recipe.method: L_H2O/L_IR (using L_IR,tot and L_IR,SF) and H2O/CO, OH+/H2O ratios compared with ULIRGs, SMGs, AGN and Mrk231
assumptions: Only sources with the same H2O transition are compared

evidence.quote: a line luminosity of $L_{\rm OH^+(1_{1}-0_{1})} = 6.92\times10^8 L_\odot$
We find that the H$_2$O emission of W0149$+$2350 extends across $2.3\pm0.6$ kpc
while the CO(9$-$8) emission extends across $3.3\pm0.5$ kpc
The OH$^+$ is extended across $9.3\pm2.1$ kpc
similar to the CO($9-8$) emission extending over $5.7\pm0.6$ kpc
while the H$_2$O is more compact covering $3.0\pm0.6$ kpc
